items.title: Call to Order
Reconvene to Open Session / Roll Call
Report Out on Closed Session from April 22, 2026
Welcome / Pledge of Allegiance
Changes to the Agenda
Approval of the Agenda (Action Required)
Public Comment

publicComments.name: Jenny and Archer
publicComments.summary: Two Orion students expressed concern about the proposed 3rd/4th grade combo class, arguing it would result in unequal instruction and asking for two dedicated 3rd grade classes.

publicComments.name: Allison Rhodes
publicComments.summary: Representing Clifford Elementary teachers, she presented a petition outlining concerns about multiple combination classrooms, lack of instructional aide support, impact on student achievement, and disproportionate numbers of IEP/504 students, requesting elimination of combo classes.

publicComments.name: Andrew Chan
publicComments.summary: Parent of four future Orion students, praised the Mandarin Immersion program and argued that a 3rd/4th combo class would dilute the critical 3rd grade immersion experience, proposing instead to recruit enough students to justify two full 3rd grade classes.

publicComments.name: Richard Palm
publicComments.summary: Parent of two Orion MI students shared his daughters' positive experiences in the program and expressed concern that a combo class would harm his younger daughter who needs hands-on attention.

publicComments.name: Jason Madsen
publicComments.summary: Speaking on behalf of many 2nd grade MI families, he described the proposed combo class structure, expressed concern about reduced Mandarin instructional consistency and quality for students with IEPs/504s, and asked the district to provide two dedicated 3rd grade classes.

publicComments.name: Ann Law
publicComments.summary: Twin mother in the Orion MI program asked the district to reconsider the combo class proposal as it would force her to choose which twin gets the combo class experience versus a standard one.

publicComments.name: Julia Redesnerda
publicComments.summary: Parent of a rising 3rd grader and incoming TK student in the MI program advocated for two fully funded, fully staffed 3rd grade classrooms, warning that the combo proposal could discourage families from staying in the program.

publicComments.name: Heidi Glasser
publicComments.summary: Long-time MI program parent who recalled the program's growth since the 2015 pilot year urged the board to invest in the program's sustainability so parents don't face the difficult choice between MI and North Star Academy.

publicComments.name: Jasper Chen
publicComments.summary: Parent of an Orion 2nd grader and TK student praised Principal Winnie's leadership and echoed the call to build the enrollment pipeline rather than create compromises that might cause parents to leave the MI program.

items.title: Labor Association Comments

publicComments.name: Maria Stockton
publicComments.summary: CSEA President requested the reinstatement of a joint calendar committee (CSEA, RCTA, and district representatives) to collaboratively determine the school calendar, expressing concern that classified staff were being excluded from decisions about start/end dates.
